chunks: I seek Thy protection from becoming destitute despite Thy riches, from being misguided despite Thy guidance, from being molested in Thy realm, and from being humiliated while authority rests with Thee.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things one seeks protection from in this supplication from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha, this supplication reflects the Shia emphasis on *tawhid* by seeking protection not just from external hardships, but from the spiritual contradiction of being deprived of God’s inherent attributes despite His omnipotence. It underscores the believer's reliance on divine justice (*adl*) and sovereignty (*sultan*), framing personal dignity as inextricably linked to the recognition of God's authority.
